question: Should an installed Claude CLI implicitly authorize autoreview to send every default review to Claude alongside Codex, or must the cross-provider panel remain opt-in?
rationale: The branch intentionally changes provider selection, data disclosure, cost, and latency for existing users; tests cannot determine whether that compatibility tradeoff matches the intended product contract.

options.title: Keep panel opt-in
options.body: Preserve Codex as the no-configuration default and require an explicit reviewer or environment selection to add Claude.

options.title: Approve panel default
options.body: Accept installed CLI availability as consent, while documenting the provider, cost, disclosure, degradation, and upgrade behavior prominently.

options.title: Reconcile the panel PRs
options.body: Pause this branch until maintainers choose which portions of this PR and https://github.com/openclaw/agent-skills/pull/90 define the canonical panel contract.

recommendation.title: Keep panel opt-in
recommendation.body: Preserve Codex as the no-configuration default and require an explicit reviewer or environment selection to add Claude.

likelyOwner.reason: The feature history points to steipete as the autoreview introducer and a recent contributor to its default behavior and review contract.
